checks.name: Storage is not public
checks.description: Public access blocks are on for accounts and buckets, and no bucket, snapshot or image is shared with everyone.
checks.remediation: Turn on block public access for the account and remove public sharing from the listed buckets, snapshots and images.

controls.rationale: One of the hardening items the CIS benchmark sets: public storage is blocked. The rest of the baseline and its approved exceptions stay with cloud.hardening_baseline and people.
Shows the high risk regression 'public storage' is absent today. Alerting on it, and investigating each alert, are separate.

provider_notes.aws: Account level S3 block public access has all four flags on (or each bucket does); no bucket policy status is public; EBS snapshot and AMI block public access is on per Region; no EBS snapshot, AMI or RDS snapshot is shared with 'all'. Needs s3:GetAccountPublicAccessBlock, s3:GetBucketPublicAccessBlock, s3:GetBucketPolicyStatus, ec2:DescribeSnapshotAttribute, ec2:GetSnapshotBlockPublicAccessState, ec2:GetImageBlockPublicAccessState, ec2:DescribeImages, rds:DescribeDBSnapshotAttributes. A missing block configuration is a real finding, not an error.
provider_notes.azure: Every storage account has allowBlobPublicAccess false, or publicNetworkAccess Disabled. That the account flag blocks anonymous access for every container is Microsoft's documented behaviour, but the page was not re read this round (unverified).
provider_notes.gcp: Every bucket has publicAccessPrevention enforced (or inherits it from the organisation policy), and no resource has a binding to allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers unless recorded as public by design. Bindings come from Security Reviewer (searchAllIamPolicies). The binding half reaches any resource type, not only storage.

checks.population: AWS: account level block public access per account, every S3 bucket, owned EBS snapshots and AMIs, and RDS snapshots, in every in scope account and enabled Region. Azure: every storage account in every in scope subscription. Google Cloud: every bucket and every IAM binding in every in scope project.
checks.predicate: Public access is blocked at account or bucket level and nothing is shared with everyone, using each cloud's fields in provider_notes. A resource recorded in Verity as public by design (with a reason) passes.
checks.period: Settings are read at each run; the daily result history is the Type 2 record.
checks.empty_population: not_applicable only when every account, subscription or project and every enabled Region was read and none holds storage of these types; any unread scope is insufficient_information.
checks.notes: No artifact names this check today. aws.md writes 'NEED cloud_infrastructure: a dated export of public storage settings' and says it would otherwise sit under alerts-on-drift-that-were-investigated; the artifact key here is an extractor placeholder (see artifacts_proposed). It maps only to NS-04 and LM-03, not to a data protection control; the merger may want to check whether a DM control fits better. The Google Cloud predicate also judges allUsers bindings on any resource, which is wider than storage. Related gcp.md need: preventive organisation level guardrails that block public storage (see decisions). Not a duplicate of any existing check.

checks.name: Cloud console users use two factor
checks.description: Every cloud user who can sign in to the console with a password has a second factor.
checks.remediation: Add a second factor for each listed user, or move them to single sign on and remove their password.

controls.rationale: The cloud console side of 'every user has a second factor'. The identity provider covers everyone who signs in through it.

provider_notes.aws: From the IAM credential report (iam:GenerateCredentialReport, iam:GetCredentialReport): password_enabled and mfa_active per user. Identity Center users only partly: their MFA settings are read where the API allows (unverified).
provider_notes.azure: Not applicable: people sign in through Entra ID; see entra-id.md (idp checks).
provider_notes.gcp: Not in the first version: people sign in through the identity provider (Workspace or Cloud Identity).

checks.population: IAM users with a console password in every in scope account; Identity Center users where the API shows MFA settings (unverified).
checks.predicate: Every IAM user with password_enabled TRUE has mfa_active TRUE.
checks.period: Read at each run; daily history. The credential report can be regenerated at most every 4 hours.
checks.empty_population: Shared AWS rule: not_applicable only when every account was read and no IAM user has a password; an unread account is insufficient_information.
checks.notes: Overlap review. Not a duplicate of cloud.root_account_mfa: that check covers only root and break glass accounts and also requires no root access keys (and accepts centralized root access management); this one covers every other IAM user with a console password. Not a duplicate of idp.mfa_enforced, which covers people signing in through the identity provider. Recommendation: keep as its own key rather than fold into cloud.root_account_mfa, because folding would change a shipped predicate and population. Fill: aws.md adds it with cloud.root_account_mfa to second-factor-enforcement-and-enrolled-users (IAM-03.B, IAM-03.C), partial, the AWS side only.

checks.name: Unused cloud credentials are disabled
checks.description: No cloud password or active access key has gone unused for longer than the set number of days.
checks.remediation: Disable or delete the listed passwords and keys.

controls.rationale: Inactive machine credentials are found (IAM-10.E). The review of the inventory stays with people.
Leftover cloud accounts of leavers show up. Matching them to the leaver list is separate.

provider_notes.aws: Credential report password_last_used and access_key_N_last_used_date, plus iam:ListAccessKeys and iam:GetAccessKeyLastUsed for keys beyond the first two per user.
provider_notes.azure: Not applicable: people sign in through Entra ID; see entra-id.md.
provider_notes.gcp: Not in the first version: key last use was not verified this round; people sign in through the identity provider.

checks.population: IAM users' console passwords and active access keys in every in scope account.
checks.predicate: No password or active key went unused for longer than the setting.
checks.period: Read at each run; daily history.
checks.empty_population: not_applicable only when every account was read and holds no IAM password or active key; an unread account is insufficient_information.
checks.notes: Overlap review. Not a duplicate of cloud.machine_credentials_rotated, which judges key age (younger than 90 days), not use, and does not cover passwords. A similar predicate exists on the identity provider side (entra-id.md uses idp.no_inactive_accounts); keep separate keys per capability, since checks are written per capability. Fill: aws.md adds it to records-of-rotation-or-review (IAM-10.D, IAM-10.E), which already lists cloud.machine_credentials_rotated; IAM-10.E asks that accounts with no recent sign in were disabled, which fits.

checks.name: Cloud access list is exported
checks.description: The complete list of cloud users, roles people can assume and their assignments is read for every account in scope.
checks.remediation: Connect every account in scope so the list is complete.

controls.rationale: The complete account list a review starts from (IAM-02.B). The review and its sign off are people's.

provider_notes.aws: IAM users (credential report), roles people can assume, Identity Center users, groups and account assignments (sso and identitystore list calls, from the management or delegated administrator account), per account.
provider_notes.azure: All role assignments at every in scope scope with principal type, read completely for every subscription; principal names resolved from the Entra ID connector when it is connected.
provider_notes.gcp: The complete organisation wide binding list from searchAllIamPolicies, dated.

checks.population: IAM users, roles assumable by people, Identity Center users and assignments per AWS account; role assignments per Azure subscription and management group; IAM bindings across the Google Cloud organisation.
checks.predicate: The full list was read for every in scope account, subscription or project (a population export, like idp.access_list_exported).
checks.period: Weekly; each result is the dated list.
checks.empty_population: pass only when complete; insufficient_information when any account, subscription or project was not read; error on a denied call.
checks.notes: Same predicate as the existing idp.access_list_exported (identity_provider) and the proposed vcs.access_list_exported (version_control), on a different capability. Recommendation: keep three keys, one per capability, as the AUTHORING section 3 prefix rule asks. A single key spanning capabilities would let an identity provider export pass while the cloud or code system list is missing, because one connected provider per capability is enough. Mapping inconsistency for the merger: idp.access_list_exported maps IAM-02 and IAM-09, vcs.access_list_exported maps IAM-02, IAM-07 and IAM-12, and this key maps only IAM-02 although its rows are also the privileged cloud roles (IAM-07) and leftover leaver accounts (IAM-12); consider aligning. aws.md says it fills account-list-export in full for the AWS accounts in scope, and adds it with cloud.environments_separated to cloud-accounts-and-production-access (partial). aws.md section 8 also uses it to show which accounts were read (one account is not the estate).

checks.name: Network traffic is logged
checks.description: Every production network that has at least one network interface keeps an active flow log.
checks.remediation: Turn on flow logs for the listed networks.

controls.rationale: Network traffic reaches a log store. Reviewing it is separate.

provider_notes.aws: ec2:DescribeFlowLogs: each VPC has an active flow log (any destination) for ALL or REJECT traffic.
provider_notes.azure: Network Watcher flow logs: each virtual network (or NSG) in a production subscription with at least one network interface has an enabled flow log.
provider_notes.gcp: Subnets in production projects have flow logs on; the field was not verified this round.

checks.population: VPCs (AWS), virtual networks or NSGs (Azure), subnets (Google Cloud) in production accounts, subscriptions or projects that hold at least one network interface.
checks.predicate: Each has an active flow log; on AWS for ALL or REJECT traffic, to any destination.
checks.period: Read at each run; daily history.
checks.empty_population: not_applicable only when every production scope was read and holds no network with an interface.
checks.notes: Not a duplicate of cloud.audit_logging (control plane activity). Fill conflict: aws.md adds it with cloud.audit_logging to evidence-logs-are-reviewed (LM-02.B, partial: sources reach a store, review is people's), while azure.md says evidence-logs-are-reviewed stays person and gcp.md does not list it. Depends on production marks per account, subscription or project.

checks.name: Backups succeed
checks.description: Every failed backup in the last 30 days was followed by a good backup in time, and each database can be restored to a recent point.
checks.remediation: Fix the failing backup and confirm the next one completes.

controls.rationale: Shows backups ran and failures were followed by a good backup (BC-01.B, part of BC-01.C). The alert, ticket and cause are a person's record.

provider_notes.aws: AWS Backup ListBackupJobs (state, created after) for in scope resources, and RDS latest restorable time. Job history retention unverified.
provider_notes.azure: Recovery Services backup job history (endpoint not verified this round). SQL point in time restore is a platform feature, so SQL databases pass on retention alone.
provider_notes.gcp: Cloud SQL backup runs in the last 30 days (endpoint not verified this round).

checks.population: Backup jobs in the last 30 days for in scope resources (AWS Backup, Recovery Services, Cloud SQL backup runs); each RDS database's latest restorable time.
checks.predicate: Every failed, aborted or expired job was followed by a completed job for the same resource within the setting, and each RDS database's latest restorable time is within 24 hours.
checks.empty_population: not_applicable when AWS Backup is unused and no RDS exists (AWS); otherwise an unread scope is insufficient_information.

parameters.follow_up_hours: default 48: a failed job must be followed by a completed job within this time
parameters.restorable_time_hours: 24: RDS latest restorable time must be this recent

checks.notes: Not a duplicate of cloud.backups_enabled, which reads configuration (retention, PITR, plan coverage); this one reads operation. Fill: aws.md and azure.md add it with cloud.backups_enabled to backup-failure-alerts-and-follow-up (BC-01.B, BC-01.C), partial; gcp.md lists only cloud.backups_enabled on that artifact.

checks.name: Backups are kept apart
checks.description: Each vault that holds production backups is locked, or its backups are copied to another account or region.
checks.remediation: Lock the vault or copy backups to another account or region.

controls.rationale: The separate, immutable copy of BC-01.D. The review of restore rights is separate.

provider_notes.aws: backup:DescribeBackupVault (vault lock, minimum retention) and backup plan copy actions.
provider_notes.azure: Recovery Services vault immutability and soft delete settings; field names not verified this round.
provider_notes.gcp: Not in the first version: backup vault locks were not verified this round.

checks.population: Backup vaults holding production recovery points.
checks.predicate: Each vault is locked, or its plan copies to another account or Region.
checks.period: Read at each run; daily history.
checks.empty_population: Shared rule: not_applicable only when every production scope was read and holds no backup vault.
checks.notes: No artifact is named for this check in any of the six documents, so as proposed it changes no objective. BC-01.D is filled today through backup-policy-covering-scope-frequency-and and list-of-privileged-accounts-with-approval, neither of which is a vault settings export; the merger should pick or propose an artifact. Related azure.md and gcp.md need about Key Vault soft delete and purge protection protecting keys that protect backups (see decisions).

checks.name: A restore was tested this year
checks.description: Each type of production data store had at least one completed restore, or a restore testing plan run, in the last 12 months.
checks.remediation: Run a restore test, or set up a restore testing plan.

controls.rationale: A restore happened in the period (BC-02.B). Proving the data was complete (BC-02.C) and the times against targets (BC-02.D) stays with people.

provider_notes.aws: backup:ListRestoreJobs and backup:ListRestoreTestingPlans (operation name unverified). Not in the SecurityAudit managed policy, so the custom policy carries it.
provider_notes.azure: Not assessed: azure.md section 1 says restore tests stay with people.
provider_notes.gcp: Not assessed: gcp.md section 1 says restore tests are not proven.

checks.population: AWS Backup restore jobs and restore testing plans for production resources.
checks.predicate: At least one completed restore job, or a restore testing plan run, for each production data store type in the last 12 months.
checks.empty_population: not_applicable when AWS Backup is unused; an unread account is insufficient_information.
checks.notes: Only aws.md defines it; azure.md and gcp.md do not list it in their reuse tables and say restore tests stay with people. Fill: restore-test-plan-and-results (BC-02.B; the artifact also serves BC-02.C and BC-02.E), partial.

checks.name: Stored secrets rotate
checks.description: Each secret in the cloud secrets manager has rotation on, or was changed within the set number of days.
checks.remediation: Turn on rotation, or rotate the listed secrets and record it.

controls.rationale: Rotation on schedule (NS-09.C). Secrets held outside the secrets manager are not seen.
Integration credentials kept as secrets rotate.

provider_notes.aws: secretsmanager:ListSecrets only (never returns values): rotation enabled, rotation rules, last rotated, last changed.
provider_notes.azure: Needs the custom Key Vault metadata reader role (data actions vaults/*/read and secrets/readMetadata/action). Predicate on Azure: each enabled secret has an expiry, or was updated within the setting. Vaults on the access policy model need an access policy.
provider_notes.gcp: Secret Manager secrets with a rotation schedule, or a version newer than the setting; fields not verified this round.

checks.population: Secrets in the cloud secrets manager (Secrets Manager, Key Vault secrets, Secret Manager) in production accounts, subscriptions or projects.
checks.predicate: Each secret has rotation enabled, or was last changed within the setting. Values are never read.
checks.period: Read at each run; daily history.
checks.empty_population: not_applicable when no secret exists and every production scope was read.
checks.notes: Overlap review. Not a duplicate of cloud.secrets_managed (a secrets manager is in use, NS-09) nor of cloud.machine_credentials_rotated (provider native keys younger than 90 days: IAM access keys, service account keys, storage account keys, Azure app credentials, IAM-10). Populations, thresholds (365 versus 90 days) and controls differ, so recommend keeping it as its own key rather than folding it into either. Meaning conflict: the Azure predicate accepts 'has an expiry', but an expiry date set on a secret does not show it is rotated; AWS and Google Cloud ask for rotation on or a recent change. Recommend aligning Azure to 'rotation policy or updated within the setting'. Fill: aws.md and azure.md add it with cloud.secrets_managed to secret-store-rotation-list (NS-09.B, NS-09.C, NS-09.D, SD-11.C); aws.md says full for Secrets Manager (names and dates, no values). gcp.md lists only cloud.secrets_managed there.

checks.name: Threat findings are handled in time
checks.description: No threat finding at or above the set severity has stayed open longer than the response time.
checks.remediation: Investigate the listed findings and archive them with the outcome.

controls.rationale: No high finding sat unhandled past the response time (supports NS-05.C). The triage decision and its reason are a person's record.

provider_notes.aws: GuardDuty ListFindings and GetFindings, filtered to the severity setting and not archived. GuardDuty keeps findings about 90 days (unverified).
provider_notes.azure: Defender alerts with status Active older than the response time; alerts list path and api-version unverified this round.
provider_notes.gcp: Premium or Enterprise only: active Security Command Center findings of class threat at or above the severity setting; v2 finding field names to confirm in fixtures. On Standard the threat service is not available.

checks.population: Threat findings or alerts at or above the severity setting that are not archived or closed, from GuardDuty, Defender for Cloud or Security Command Center.
checks.predicate: None has stayed open longer than the response time setting.
checks.period: Read daily; findings open now, aged from first seen.
checks.empty_population: not_applicable when there are no findings (and the service is on and fully read); error when denied; insufficient_information when a scope was unread.
checks.notes: Not a duplicate of cloud.threat_detection (the service is on). azure.md section 5.3 leaves open whether this key widens to cover configuration rule findings with first seen and resolved times (NS-04, NS-05, NS-08, LM-03) or a new key is added; see decisions. Similar 'alerts handled in time' predicates may come from endpoint or alerting research; the merger should check for aliases there. Fill: sample-of-alerts-that-were-investigated (NS-05.C, NS-05.D, NS-05.E), partial, on all three clouds (Google Cloud on Premium or Enterprise only).

checks.name: Certificates are current
checks.description: No certificate in use has expired, or expires within 14 days without being able to renew itself.
checks.remediation: Renew or replace the listed certificates.

controls.rationale: Certificates on the cloud's front doors stay valid (NS-02.E). Certificates outside the cloud certificate store are not seen.

provider_notes.aws: ACM ListCertificates and DescribeCertificate: not after, renewal eligibility, in use by.
provider_notes.azure: Certificates in Key Vault (needs the Key Vault metadata reader role; certificate list path unverified): none expired, none expiring within 14 days without auto renewal.
provider_notes.gcp: Not in the first version: certificate stores were not verified this round.

checks.population: Certificates in use in the cloud certificate store (ACM, Key Vault certificates).
checks.predicate: None has expired, and none in use expires within the warning window without being eligible for automatic renewal.
checks.period: Read at each run; daily history.
checks.empty_population: not_applicable when no certificate exists in the store and every scope was read.
checks.notes: Not a duplicate of cloud.tls_in_transit (protocol versions). An edge or certificate check may be proposed by operations research (network edge); the merger should look for an alias there. Fill: aws.md and azure.md add it with cloud.tls_in_transit to public-endpoint-tls-scan (NS-02.B, NS-02.C, NS-02.E), partial: the listener side, not a scan of each domain.

checks.name: Removed systems are retired
checks.description: Every register asset that came from a cloud connection still exists there, or was retired in Verity within 7 days of disappearing.
checks.remediation: Retire the listed assets, or record why they stay.

controls.rationale: Keeps the register accurate as resources are removed (supports LM-01.D). The quarterly review is a person's.

provider_notes.aws: Compares assets whose source is AWS with the latest discovery (Resource Explorer or per type enumeration).
provider_notes.azure: Compares assets whose source is Azure with Resource Graph.
provider_notes.gcp: Compares assets whose source is Google Cloud with searchAllResources.

checks.population: Assets in the Verity register whose source is the connected cloud.
checks.predicate: Each asset still exists in the cloud, or is retired in Verity within the grace period after it disappeared.
checks.period: Read daily; disappearance dated by last_seen.
checks.empty_population: Shared rule: not_applicable when no asset has that source and discovery was complete.
checks.notes: Inverse of the existing assets.resources_registered (discovered resources must be in the register); not a duplicate. A resource missing from discovery is never treated as disposal proof: the check asks a person to retire it. Fill: aws.md adds it to asset-inventory (LM-01.B, LM-01.C and other objectives), which already lists assets.resources_registered. The objective it says it supports, LM-01.D, cites review-that-the-inventory-is-complete, not asset-inventory.

checks.name: Nobody bypasses branch protection
checks.description: The default branch rule applies to administrators, and nobody outside the allowed list can bypass it.
checks.remediation: Include administrators in the rule and remove bypass permissions that are not needed.

controls.rationale: The 'bypass limited' part of SD-06.C.
The emergency route is bounded to named people.

provider_notes.github: Classic protection has enforce_admins on, and every ruleset on the default branch has no bypass actors beyond the allowed list. Reads GET /repos/{o}/{r}/rulesets/{id} (Metadata) and classic protection (Administration). Error when a ruleset cannot be read.
provider_notes.gitlab: GitLab has no separate bypass list; judged from the protected branch's push and merge access levels: no role above the allowed set may push or merge without the approval rule, and no user may push directly except named automation.
provider_notes.bitbucket: Only if the owner approves D-BB-1 (admin:repository scope, which can edit restrictions): no users or groups exempted from approval and build restrictions beyond the allowed list. Under the recommended option (a) it is not read.

checks.population: The default branch policy of each in scope repository (archived and forks out by default).
checks.predicate: Administrators are bound by the rule, and no bypass actors exist other than those the customer allows in settings.
checks.period: Read daily; history is the Type 2 record. A rule turned off and on between runs is invisible without an audit log.
checks.empty_population: not_applicable for an empty repository (GitHub outcome rules); insufficient_information when the repository population was cut short.

parameters.allowed_bypass_actors: default none, or deploy automation only

checks.notes: Comes from the review of the built GitHub connector: a ruleset's bypass list is not read, so vcs.default_branch_protected can pass on a ruleset every admin bypasses. Alternative: widen vcs.default_branch_protected's predicate instead; recommend a separate key, because changing a shipped predicate changes earlier results' meaning. On GitLab this predicate is close to what vcs.default_branch_protected already tests (push access levels), so the two will often agree there. GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket all listed as planned providers in github.md section 5.2.

checks.name: New commits need a new approval
checks.description: Approvals are dismissed when new commits are pushed, or the latest push must be approved by someone else.
checks.remediation: Dismiss approvals when new commits are pushed, or require approval of the latest push.

controls.rationale: The approval covers what actually merges.
The approved change is the released change.

provider_notes.github: Classic protection or ruleset: dismiss stale approvals, or require approval of the most recent push by someone else (ruleset parameter names unverified). Needs Administration read.
provider_notes.gitlab: Premium and Ultimate only (Free fails with reason plan): reset_approvals_on_push is true, or committers cannot approve (merge_requests_disable_committers_approval).
provider_notes.bitbucket: Only with D-BB-1: the branch restriction that resets approvals when the source branch changes is on (restriction kind name unverified).

checks.population: The default branch policy of each in scope repository.
checks.predicate: Approvals are dismissed on new commits, or the latest push must be approved by someone other than its pusher.
checks.notes: Comes from the GitHub review finding that stale approvals are reported but not judged (approvals before later commits count under GitHub's rules). Related to vcs.review_required and vcs.merged_changes_reviewed but tests a different setting; keep separate. Meaning note: GitLab's accepted alternative 'committers cannot approve' is a different safeguard from resetting approvals on push; gitlab.md treats either as a pass.

checks.name: Secret pushes are blocked
checks.description: Secret scanning push protection is on for every repository in scope.
checks.remediation: Turn on push protection in the repository's security settings.

controls.rationale: Secrets are blocked before they land, not only found after.
Supports 'no secrets in source code'.

provider_notes.github: security_and_analysis.secret_scanning_push_protection (field name unverified), Administration read. Private repositories need GitHub Secret Protection (Team and Enterprise Cloud since 1 April 2025); otherwise fail with reason plan.
provider_notes.gitlab: Ultimate only (fail with reason plan otherwise): the project's secret push protection setting from the Projects API.
provider_notes.bitbucket: Not possible: Bitbucket secret scanning and its API were not confirmed; GitHub, GitLab Ultimate or a scanner is needed.

checks.predicate: Secret scanning push protection is on.
checks.notes: Overlaps the existing vcs.secret_scanning_enabled (scanning of pushes and history) as a stronger sub setting. Recommendation: keep separate, because the tier gates differ (GitLab pipeline secret detection runs on all tiers, push protection is Ultimate only) and folding it in would change a shipped predicate. Fill: added with vcs.secret_scanning_enabled and vcs.secret_alerts_closed_in_time to records-of-exposed-secrets-that-were (SD-11.B to SD-11.E, NS-09.D), partial.

checks.name: Exposed secrets are dealt with
checks.description: No secret scanning alert stays open longer than the set number of days, and every push protection bypass led to an alert that was resolved.
checks.remediation: Rotate the exposed secret, then resolve the alert as revoked.

controls.rationale: Exposed secrets were dealt with in time (SD-11.C). Rotation proof and misuse review (SD-11.D) are people's.
Supports NS-09.D.

provider_notes.github: GET /repos/{o}/{r}/secret-scanning/alerts?hide_secret=true (Secret scanning alerts read). The secret field holds the secret unless hide_secret=true; the collector always sets it and strips the field. A 404 means public repository, scanning off or not found; tell apart with security_and_analysis.
provider_notes.gitlab: Ultimate only (fail with reason plan otherwise): secret detection vulnerabilities from the vulnerability report through GraphQL (the REST API is being deprecated; field names unverified).
provider_notes.bitbucket: Not possible: no confirmed secret scanning.

checks.population: Secret scanning alerts open now or resolved in the last 30 days, in scope repositories.
checks.predicate: No alert open longer than the setting; every push protection bypass in the window has an alert that was resolved.
checks.empty_population: not_applicable when there are no alerts and scanning is on; insufficient_information when the population was cut short.
checks.notes: Practice side of the existing vcs.secret_scanning_enabled (setting); not a duplicate. Decision D-GH-2 also applies: the alternative is importing secret and dependency alerts into the Verity vulnerability register so verity.vulns.within_sla judges every source in one place.

checks.name: Dependency alerts are fixed in time
checks.description: No open dependency alert is older than the workspace's vulnerability timeframe for its severity, and each dismissal has a reason.
checks.remediation: Update or patch the dependency, or dismiss the alert with a reason.

controls.rationale: Alerts are triaged and fixed in time (SD-03.D, SD-03.E).
One finding source is fixed within the timeframes (LM-11.D).

provider_notes.github: Dependabot alerts read: state, severity, advisory (GHSA, CVE), created, dismissed with reason, fixed, auto dismissed.
provider_notes.gitlab: Ultimate only (fail with reason plan otherwise): dependency scanning vulnerabilities from the vulnerability report (GraphQL).
provider_notes.bitbucket: Not possible: Bitbucket has no native dependency alerts; a scanner (Phase 3) is needed.

checks.population: Dependency alerts open now or closed in the last 30 days, in scope repositories.
checks.predicate: No open alert is older than the workspace's timeframe for its severity (from the vulnerabilities module settings); each dismissal has a reason.
checks.empty_population: not_applicable when there are no alerts and alerts are on; insufficient_information when the population was cut short.

parameters.timeframes: per severity, read from the Verity vulnerabilities module settings

checks.notes: Practice side of the existing vcs.dependency_alerts_enabled; not a duplicate. Overlaps the existing verity.vulns.within_sla (LM-11, EP-04) in meaning: D-GH-2 asks whether to judge these alerts here (recommended now) or import them into the Verity vulnerability register so verity.vulns.within_sla judges every source (what LM-11.C asks for; a module change, spec first; recommended later). If the import is built, this key could be retired in favour of verity.vulns.within_sla. Fill: added with vcs.dependency_alerts_enabled to open-alerts-triaged-within-the-timeframe (SD-03.B, SD-03.D, SD-03.E), partial: container images are not covered.

checks.name: Code access list is exported
checks.description: The full list of organization members, owners, outside collaborators and repository admins is read for the code system.
checks.remediation: Connect every organization so the list is complete.

controls.rationale: The account list for the code system (IAM-02.B).
Owners and repository admins are the privileged accounts (IAM-07.B).
Leavers still in the organization become visible (IAM-12.E).

provider_notes.github: Organization Members read: members with role, 2fa_disabled and 2fa_insecure filters (owners only), outside collaborators, repository collaborators with admin permission.
provider_notes.gitlab: GET /groups/:id/members/all with access levels 10 to 50 (Reporter); two factor state only where the API exposes it (unverified for group Owners on GitLab.com).
provider_notes.bitbucket: read:workspace scope: workspace members and permissions (owner, collaborator, member).

checks.population: Organization (group, workspace) members with role, outside collaborators, and admins of in scope repositories.
checks.predicate: The full list was read (a population export).
checks.period: Weekly; each result is the dated list.
checks.empty_population: pass only when complete; insufficient_information otherwise; error on a denied call.
checks.notes: Same predicate as the existing idp.access_list_exported on another capability. Recommendation: keep it as its own key (prefix rule, and one connected identity provider must not stand in for the code system list). github.md says it fills account-list-export in full for the code system and list-of-privileged-accounts-with-approval partially (the approval of each grant is a person's). The observation type for members is not named in 01-evidence-model.md 1.4 (only repository, branch_rule, change, review, pipeline_run, deployment are); the merger may need a member observation type.

checks.name: Production releases were approved
checks.description: Each production deployment in the last 30 days ran from the default branch or a tag and, where reviewers are required, was approved by someone other than the person who started it.
checks.remediation: Require reviewers on the production environment and deploy only from the default branch.

controls.rationale: Each release was approved before it ran (SD-13.C) and came from a protected source (SD-13.B).
Nothing went straight to production outside the path (supports SD-12.D).

provider_notes.github: Actions read (GET .../actions/runs/{run_id}/approvals) and Deployments read. The link from a deployment to its run is unverified; insufficient_information when approvals cannot be linked. Required reviewers on private repositories are Enterprise only per current docs.
provider_notes.gitlab: Premium and Ultimate (deployment approvals, approval_summary); fail with reason plan on Free.
provider_notes.bitbucket: Not possible: Bitbucket has deployment permissions, not per deployment approvals (that no approval record exists is unverified).

checks.population: Production deployments in the last 30 days in repositories marked as deploying production.
checks.predicate: Each ran from the default branch or a tag and, where the environment requires reviewers, carries an approval by someone other than the person who triggered the run.
checks.empty_population: A repository marked as deploying with no deployment record is insufficient_information, never a pass (it may deploy from elsewhere); insufficient_information also when approvals could not be linked.
checks.notes: Overlap review. The existing ci.production_deploys_controlled judges the setting (the environment exists with reviewers or branch rules); this key judges practice per deployment, like vcs.review_required versus vcs.merged_changes_reviewed. It also reads the same population as ci.deployment_history_recorded (commit, creator, time, status; SD-13, SD-14) but adds the approval and source branch test. Recommendation: keep as its own key; do not fold into ci.production_deploys_controlled or ci.deployment_history_recorded, because each carries different controls and shipped results. Fill: added to deployment-history-for-a-sample-of (SD-12.D, SD-13.B, SD-13.C, SD-13.E), which already lists ci.deployment_history_recorded.

existing_implementations.note: S3 buckets, RDS instances, clusters and snapshots, EBS volumes and snapshots, EFS, DynamoDB, plus EBS encryption by default per Region. S3 always passes since SSE-S3 became default on 5 January 2023; objects written earlier are not proven and older buckets carry a note.

AWS front doors: ALB and NLB listeners, CloudFront, API Gateway custom domains (field unverified). No listener policy allowing TLS 1.0 or 1.1; HTTP listeners only redirect. The API and CloudFormation default ELBSecurityPolicy-2016-08 allows TLS 1.0 and 1.1, so code built listeners often fail. Internal traffic (NS-02.D) and HSTS (NS-02.C) are not visible.

Security groups attached to an interface and NACLs: no all protocol rule from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0; open internet ports only from the setting (default 80, 443) on groups attached to a load balancer; each VPC's default security group has no rules.

No rule opens 22, 3389 or a database port (default 1433, 1521, 3306, 5432, 6379, 9200, 27017) to 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0; no RDS instance publicly accessible. Recorded exceptions (reason, approver, expiry) pass until expiry.

Through Security Hub CSPM: the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark (v5.0.0 recommended) enabled in each account and Region with no FAILED active findings except recorded exceptions. Needs AWS Config. Security Hub CSPM off is error (the customer chose another source). Up to 18 hours to first findings: a fresh standard is insufficient_information. Server and container baselines not covered. Phase question D-AWS-1.
A GuardDuty detector exists and is ENABLED in every in scope account and Region. GuardDuty off is a fail.

Enabled symmetric customer managed keys with AWS generated material: automatic rotation on, period at most the setting (365 days). AWS managed keys not counted; asymmetric, HMAC and custom key store keys listed as needing manual rotation records.

Databases sit in subnets with no internet gateway route, are not publicly accessible, and no production workload runs in a default VPC. A configuration reading, not the segmentation test NS-07.D asks for.

Shows a secrets manager is in use in each production account (a secret accessed in the last 90 days). Cannot show no secret sits in configuration, because those APIs return values; that half comes from vcs.secret_scanning_enabled and a person.
RDS retention at least the setting (default 7 days); DynamoDB point in time recovery on; EFS and EBS in an AWS Backup plan selection with enough retention.
Production RDS instances and clusters each have a free storage and a CPU alarm with actions enabled; EBS backed instances later.

A multi Region or organization trail is logging, records management read and write events, has log file validation on, delivered in the last 24 hours, and its bucket blocks public access and keeps logs at least the setting (default 365 days).

Recording yes: AWS Config records all supported types in every Region (or an organization aggregator covers them) with a working delivery channel. Alerts partly: alarms on the CIS metric filter set (security group, NACL, IAM policy, trail changes), which Verity reads itself because CIS v5.0.0 leaves them to manual checks.

Root has MFA and no access keys, or the account has no root credentials under centralized root access management (a pass, not an empty population). A virtual device is noted; hardware or passkey preferred.

IAM users, groups, roles (not service linked) and Identity Center permission sets with assignments: no AdministratorAccess or * on * without a recorded need (owner, reason, review date); recorded break glass roles pass.
Every active IAM access key (credential report plus ListAccessKeys, because the report shows only two keys per user) younger than the setting (default 90 days).
Needs the customer to give each account a role (production, staging, development, shared): at least one production account, none marked both production and lower. Error when roles not set. Weekly.
Buckets and ECR repositories the customer marks as build output: bucket versioning Enabled, ECR tags immutable. Error when none marked.
Buckets and log groups marked with a retention class have expiration or retention no longer than the class's period. Weekly.

Resource Explorer (indexes per Region and an aggregator needed) or per type enumeration: EC2, RDS, S3, DynamoDB, EFS, load balancers, Lambda by name only, ECR, EKS; matched on ARN as external_id or excluded with a reason.

Storage accounts are always encrypted (key source and infrastructure encryption recorded); every SQL database has TDE Enabled; managed disks report encryption type (Resource Graph field name unverified).
Storage accounts (minimumTlsVersion TLS1_2 or later, HTTPS only) and SQL servers (minimalTlsVersion 1.2 or later) only. App Service, Front Door and Application Gateway are a later increment.

Inbound NSG allow rules with source *, Internet, 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 and port *; open ports only from the setting. Subnets and interfaces with no NSG are listed for review (Azure behaviour without an NSG unverified).
NSG rules and SQL server firewall rules; a 0.0.0.0 to 255.255.255.255 SQL rule fails; the 0.0.0.0 'allow Azure services' rule is a finding with its own reason. Exceptions pass until expiry.

Two routes: Defender CSPM (paid) with the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations standard in regulatory compliance, or a free CIS or Microsoft cloud security benchmark policy initiative with no non compliant resources. Secure score is context only, never a pass. Error when neither route is set up; without Defender CSPM it must use the initiative or fail with reason plan (D-AZ-3).
For every resource type present with a Defender plan (servers, storage, SQL, Key Vault, Resource Manager at least), that plan's pricingTier is Standard. Plan names to confirm in fixtures.

Needs the custom Key Vault metadata reader role (error without it). Enabled RSA and EC keys have a rotation policy within the setting (365 days) or a current version younger than it. Vaults on the access policy model are insufficient until an access policy is added.
SQL servers, storage accounts and key vaults marked as data stores have publicNetworkAccess Disabled, or a recorded public need. A configuration reading only.
At least one key vault holds secrets in each production subscription. Secrets in app settings are not visible without reading values.

SQL short term retentionDays at least the setting (7); each production VM is a protected item of a Recovery Services vault with enough retention. PostgreSQL and MySQL flexible servers follow when their fields are verified.
Not in the first version, not a permanent limit: Azure Monitor metric alerts exist but the alert list API was not verified this round. BC-04 stays with people until added.

A subscription diagnostic setting sends at least Administrative, Security and Policy to a Log Analytics workspace with retentionInDays at least the setting (365), or to storage kept that long. Without one the activity log lasts 90 days and the check fails.

Recording by design (activity log); passes when enabled activity log alerts cover NSG and rule changes, policy assignment changes, SQL firewall rule changes and security solution changes (CIS set; operation names to confirm).

Not applicable: Azure has no root user. Owners and Global Administrators are Entra identities judged by idp.mfa_enforced and idp.admin_mfa_phishing_resistant (entra-id.md). Result is not_applicable with that reason.

Role assignments at management group and subscription scope: no Owner, Contributor, User Access Administrator, RBAC Administrator or custom role with * actions without a recorded need; break glass passes when recorded.

Storage account keys where allowSharedKeyAccess is true (keyCreationTime or keyPolicy within 90 days). The app registration secrets and certificates half needs optional Graph Application.Read.All; insufficient when not granted and app credentials are in scope.
Needs the customer's subscription environment roles; weekly.
Storage accounts marked as build output: isVersioningEnabled true and blob soft delete on.
Storage accounts marked with a retention class: a management policy deletes blobs no later than the period.

Resource Graph types (VMs, scale sets, SQL servers and databases, storage, key vaults, AKS, App Service, container registries, public IPs); matched on the ARM resource id as cloud_resource_id and external_id. More than 10,000 visible subscriptions is insufficient_information.

Buckets, Cloud SQL, persistent disks and BigQuery datasets pass on Google's default encryption (key source recorded); a store whose customer managed key is disabled or destroyed fails. Default encryption shows no customer decision (NS-01.C).
Cloud SQL sslMode refuses unencrypted connections (enum values to confirm; requireSsl as fallback). Load balancer SSL policies are a later increment.

Enabled INGRESS allow firewall and hierarchical policy rules: none from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 covers all protocols or ports; internet ports only from the setting. Default network's permissive rules listed separately.
Firewall rules plus Cloud SQL instances with ipv4Enabled and 0.0.0.0/0 in authorizedNetworks. Exceptions pass until expiry.
Premium or Enterprise tier only: no active Security Health Analytics finding mapped to the CIS Google Cloud benchmark open except recorded exceptions. On Standard it fails with reason plan (D-GCP-2).
Premium or Enterprise tier only: Event Threat Detection enabled at the organisation. Standard or SCC not active fails with reason plan.
Enabled symmetric ENCRYPT_DECRYPT keys: rotationPeriod set and at most 365 days, nextRotationTime in the future. Asymmetric keys listed for manual records.
Production Cloud SQL instances have ipv4Enabled false (private IP only) or a recorded public need. Not a segmentation test.
Secret Manager holds at least one secret in each production project (asset inventory). Secrets in configuration are not visible.
Production Cloud SQL: backups enabled, retained backups at least 7, point in time recovery or binary logging on. Persistent disk snapshot schedules later.
Partly, and not in the first version: an enabled alert policy covering disk and CPU of each production Cloud SQL instance; metric filter matching still to be designed.

Admin Activity logs are always written and kept 400 days in _Required, which meets the 365 day default. Longer retention or Data Access logs on named services need an organisation sink to a bucket with that retention and auditConfigs.
Recording by Admin Activity logs; passes when log based metrics with enabled alert policies exist for firewall, IAM policy, custom role and Cloud SQL configuration changes (filters to confirm).
Not applicable: no root user. Organisation super administrators are Workspace or Cloud Identity accounts judged by the identity provider checks in google-workspace.md.

All bindings from searchAllIamPolicies: no user or group holds roles/owner, roles/editor, organizationAdmin, iam.securityAdmin or a custom role granting *.setIamPolicy broadly, without a recorded need.
USER_MANAGED enabled service account keys with validAfterTime within 90 days; not_applicable when none (the default on organisations created since 3 May 2024).
Needs the customer's project environment roles; weekly.
Buckets marked as build output have versioning enabled.
Buckets marked with a retention class have a lifecycle delete rule no later than the period.

searchAllResources types (Compute instances, GKE, Cloud SQL, buckets, BigQuery datasets, Cloud Run, Cloud Functions, Artifact Registry); matched on the full resource name. Projects outside the organisation are invisible.
Built. Classic protection or a ruleset blocks direct and force pushes. The ruleset bypass list is not read, so it can pass on a ruleset every admin bypasses (vcs.protection_bypass_limited proposed).
Built.
Built. Passes when any context is required (a lint job counts); the required contexts are to be printed on the result.
Built. Merged pull requests only (last decision per reviewer), so direct pushes are not seen: a pass means every pull request was reviewed, not every change.
Built and plan aware: private repositories need GitHub Secret Protection (sold to Team and Enterprise Cloud since 1 April 2025), else fail with reason plan.
Built. Dependabot alerts on all plans (unverified for every plan).
Built. Personal accounts cannot require two factor: not_applicable. Proposal: add 2fa_insecure counts to the evidence when visible.

Feasible, not built (checks.json implementations is empty): default setup configured or a default branch analysis in the last 30 days, for repositories with a supported language (list unverified). Private repositories need GitHub Code Security, else fail with reason plan.

Feasible, needs a Verity record and the links primitive between a task and an external change. Population: unapproved merges, rule suite bypasses (Administration read, up to a month), and direct pushes only if D-GH-3 grants Contents read (recommended no, so pushes outside rulesets are not seen). Insufficient when rule suites cannot be read. Review window setting default 5 working days.

Feasible: every required context concluded success on the merged head commit before merged_at; with none required, at least one check ran and none failed. The Checks permission exists only for a GitHub App. Insufficient when the rate floor is reached.

Feasible: the production environment exists and has required reviewers (with prevent_self_review) or allows deployment only from protected branches or named branch and tag rules. Required reviewers on private repositories are Enterprise only per current docs (sources disagree); a Team customer passes through the branch rule and the evidence says no person approved.
Feasible: each production deployment in 30 days has commit, ref, creator, time and a final status. A repository marked as deploying with no deployment record is insufficient_information.
All tiers. Stricter than GitHub by design: push access must be No one or named users, groups or deploy keys; a role allowed to push (Developers, Maintainers) fails. Force push off.
Premium and Ultimate only; Free cannot require approvals and fails with reason plan. Predicate also requires that authors cannot approve their own changes.
'Pipelines must succeed' on and skipped pipelines do not count as success (tier unverified).

All tiers: the approvals endpoint gives each approver and approved_at. It shows current approvals only (a withdrawn approval disappears); committer approvals count unless the project bars them, and the evidence says which.

Pipeline secret detection: the latest default branch pipeline in 30 days ran a job that produced a secret detection report (all tiers). Proves a job ran, not coverage; results appear in the vulnerability report only on Ultimate. Insufficient when no pipeline ran.
The latest default branch pipeline produced a dependency scanning report; tier unverified (believed Ultimate for results); fail with reason plan where not offered.
All tiers: require_two_factor_authentication on the top level group; the grace period is printed.
The latest default branch pipeline produced a SAST report (tier unverified).
Default branch commits are readable with read_api, so direct pushes (commits with no merge request) are found without a new permission, unlike GitHub.
The merge request's head pipeline for the merged SHA finished success before merged_at.

Premium and Ultimate (protected environments): environment with tier production is protected, deploy access limited to allowed users, groups or roles, and at least one approval required. Free fails with reason plan.
All tiers: SHA, ref, user, created and finished times and final status; insufficient for a deploying project with no records.

Only if the owner approves D-BB-1 (admin:repository:bitbucket, which can edit branch restrictions). Under the recommended option (a) it is error 'permission not granted' and the setting stays with a person's dated export.
Only with D-BB-1. Merge checks are enforced only on Premium ('Prevent a merge with unresolved merge checks'); Standard and Free fail with reason plan.
Only with D-BB-1, and Premium to enforce passing builds.
All plans with read:pullrequest: an approval by a participant other than the author, dated before the merge (approval date from activity, field unverified).
Bitbucket secret scanning and its API were not confirmed (unverified); another provider or a person.
No native dependency alerts; another source (scanner, Phase 3).
Not until a readable setting is confirmed (workspace two step enforcement exists on a paid plan, API unverified). The identity provider covers it when sign in is through Atlassian Guard or SSO.
No native code scanning.
Yes for unapproved merges; direct pushes (main branch commits with no pull request) depend on a commit to pull request lookup endpoint that is unverified.
read:pullrequest and read:pipeline: every build status on the merged source commit was SUCCESSFUL before the merge, and at least one exists.
Deployment permissions (who and which branches may deploy) are Premium; whether the API exposes them is unverified, error when not readable; fail with reason plan below Premium.
Deployments to Production type environments in 30 days with commit, state and time; the person or trigger only where the pipeline records it. Insufficient for deploying repositories with no records.

downgrades.reason: The encryption standard, the key type per data class (NS-01.C) and the 'fixed and recorded' half of NS-01.D need people. Default encryption on S3, Azure Storage and Google Cloud shows no customer decision.

downgrades.source: connectors/aws.md (5.1, D-AWS-4); connectors/azure.md (5.1, D-AZ-4); connectors/gcp.md (5.1, D-GCP-3)

downgrades.reason: Investigation of each alert (LM-03.C) is a person's record; alerting is also only partly covered on every cloud.
downgrades.source: connectors/aws.md (5.1, D-AWS-4); connectors/azure.md (5.1, D-AZ-4); connectors/gcp.md (5.1, D-GCP-3)

decisions.question: CIS hardening benchmarks are Phase 3.2 in docs/product/delivery-plan.md. Ship cloud.hardening_baseline (a read of Security Hub CSPM results) in Phase 2 as part of 'AWS core cloud', or hold it for Phase 3? Also whether Security Hub CSPM off stays an error of cloud.hardening_baseline.
options: Ship in Phase 2 as a read of the customer's own Security Hub CSPM results
decisions.recommendation: Ship it in Phase 2 as a read of the customer's Security Hub CSPM results, and say plainly that Verity does not run its own benchmark.
decisions.source: connectors/aws.md, Decisions for the owner, D-AWS-1 (and section 8)

decisions.question: Which identity does Verity use to call sts:AssumeRole, given Verity runs on Contabo, not AWS?
options: Long lived IAM user key in a Verity owned AWS account, in the runtime secret store, rotated
IAM Roles Anywhere with an X.509 certificate (needs a private CA; not researched this round)
decisions.recommendation: Start with the key in the runtime secret store, rotated every 90 days, and plan Roles Anywhere.

decisions.question: Which policy does the Verity role carry by default?
options: Custom least privilege policy (Verity managed, exactly the calls checks make; needs a customer approved stack update for each new call)
AWS managed SecurityAudit plus an explicit Deny on lambda:GetFunction, lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration, lambda:ListFunctions, ecs:DescribeTaskDefinition, cloudtrail:LookupEvents
decisions.recommendation: The custom least privilege policy. None of the competitors read offers this by default, which is a trust claim Verity can make.

decisions.topic: Full mappings where people's records remain (all clouds)
decisions.question: Change four existing full mappings to partial: cloud.encryption_at_rest to NS-01, cloud.admin_ports_closed to NS-08, cloud.config_changes_recorded to LM-03, cloud.environments_separated to SD-12?
decisions.recommendation: Change all four to partial (authoring rule 5), for every cloud.
decisions.source: connectors/aws.md D-AWS-4; connectors/azure.md D-AZ-4; connectors/gcp.md D-GCP-3

decisions.question: One external ID per Verity workspace, or one per AWS account (AWS's stated preference for multi tenant services, harder with StackSets)?
decisions.recommendation: Per workspace, with the role ARN and account checked on every assume.

decisions.question: One Verity multi tenant app shared with the Entra ID connector, or a customer owned app registration per connection?
options: Shared Verity multi tenant app with a certificate (one consent, no customer secret)
Customer owned single tenant app registration with a Verity generated certificate
decisions.recommendation: Shared multi tenant app with a certificate. Workload identity federation is a later option.

decisions.question: Ship a custom 'Key Vault metadata reader' role template instead of asking for built in Key Vault Reader, which also allows classic alert rule and support ticket writes?
For cloud.hardening_baseline on Azure, require Defender CSPM (paid) for CIS, or also accept a free CIS or Microsoft cloud security benchmark policy initiative?
options: Accept the free policy initiative too
Accept both, chosen by the customer's hardening standard
decisions.recommendation: Accept both; the customer's hardening standard names which.

decisions.question: Workload identity federation with a Verity token issuer (works on default new organisations), Verity's own service account (needs an iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains exception), or a customer service account key (needs an iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation exception)?
decisions.recommendation: Federation. Build the OIDC issuer once and reuse it for Google Cloud, Azure and AWS.

decisions.question: Treat Security Command Center Standard as fail with reason plan for cloud.hardening_baseline and cloud.threat_detection?
Build the Verity GitHub App now, and under which GitHub organization, given the November 2026 incident on Verity's GitHub branches?
options: Build now under a newly hardened Verity organization
Keep the fine grained token only
decisions.recommendation: Yes, build it: it removes the leaver problem and personal repository noise. The owner organization needs its own hardening first.

decisions.topic: Where dependency and secret alerts are judged
decisions.question: Judge Dependabot and secret scanning alerts in GitHub checks (vcs.dependency_alerts_within_sla, vcs.secret_alerts_closed_in_time), or import them into the Verity vulnerability register so verity.vulns.within_sla judges every source in one place (what LM-11.C asks for; a module change, spec first)?
decisions.recommendation: The check now, the import later.

decisions.topic: GitHub Contents read for direct pushes
decisions.question: Direct push detection needs Contents read, which can read source code. Accept it?
options: No: rely on rule suites (Administration read) and say on the result that pushes outside rulesets are not seen
Yes: read default branch commits not linked to a pull request

decisions.question: Count in scope repositories as assets (GitHub as an asset_discovery provider), so SD-06.B, SD-03.B and SD-11.B can test 'every repository is in scope' against the register? GitHub is not an asset_discovery provider in capabilities.json today. github.md writes it as 'NEED asset_discovery: the in scope repository list with exclusions is the repository population these objectives test'.
options: Add github (and by extension gitlab, bitbucket) as asset_discovery providers
Keep repositories out of the asset register

decisions.question: Maintainer by default (reads settings) with Owner as an opt in for audit events. Both can read more than Verity uses (files, CI variables). Accept, or wait for fine grained tokens (availability unverified)?
options: Accept Maintainer default, Owner opt in

decisions.question: Support GitLab.com Free through a group service account's personal access token, or require Premium (group access tokens)?
options: Support Free through a service account
decisions.recommendation: Support them through a service account.

decisions.topic: Self managed GitLab behind a firewall
decisions.question: Are self managed instances behind a firewall in Phase 2 scope (the customer allowlists Verity's egress address), or later?

decisions.topic: Bitbucket branch restrictions need an admin scope
decisions.question: Reading branch restrictions needs admin:repository:bitbucket, which can edit them; no read only scope exists (BCLOUD-24231 not confirmed shipped). Which option?
options: (a) Do not read them: merge gate settings stay with people, Bitbucket proves practice only
(b) Offer it as an opt in with an ADR, a GET only collector and a warning
(c) Ask Atlassian and revisit if a read scope ships

decisions.question: Support repository access tokens one by one, or require Premium workspace access tokens?

decisions.topic: NEED: dated export of storage versioning (reconciliation)
decisions.question: aws.md writes 'NEED cloud_infrastructure: a dated export of storage versioning' because cloud.storage_versioned has no artifact for SD-07.D other than the design document. azure.md and gcp.md instead add cloud.storage_versioned to integrity-check-results (SD-07.B, SD-07.C, SD-07.D). Use the existing artifact or add one?
options: Add a new storage versioning export artifact
decisions.source: connectors/aws.md section 6; connectors/azure.md and connectors/gcp.md section 6

decisions.topic: NEED: dated export of public storage settings (reconciliation)
decisions.question: cloud.storage_public_access_blocked has no artifact. Put it under alerts-on-drift-that-were-investigated, or add a new public exposure export?

decisions.topic: NEED: encryption keys cannot be destroyed at once (reconciliation)
decisions.question: Match or add a key for 'every key vault or key ring that holds keys, secrets or certificates protects them from immediate destruction': Azure Key Vault soft delete and purge protection (enableSoftDelete, enablePurgeProtection, read already), Google Cloud KMS scheduled destruction of at least a setting (destroyScheduledDuration, read already).
options: New cloud key (for example a keys_protected_from_deletion predicate)
decisions.source: connectors/azure.md 5.3 (for NS-06.D, NS-06.E via key-rotation-records, and BC-01 for keys that protect backups); connectors/gcp.md 5.3 (NS-06.D, NS-06.E)

decisions.topic: NEED: threat detection notifies a named contact (reconciliation)
decisions.question: Match or add a key for 'the threat detection service notifies a named security contact or an on call route for high severity alerts' (Defender securityContacts, Security Command Center notification configs). It shows someone is told, not that anyone acted.
decisions.source: connectors/azure.md 5.3 and connectors/gcp.md 5.3 (NS-05.C operating side of procedure-for-responding-to-threat-detection, LM-09)

decisions.topic: NEED: configuration rule findings with first seen and resolved times (reconciliation)
decisions.question: The coverage need 'configuration rule findings are listed with first seen and resolved times, and each open past the response time is flagged' (NS-04, NS-05, NS-08, LM-03): widen cloud.threat_findings_triaged to posture findings, or add a new key? Defender assessments give status per resource, but a first seen time was not confirmed.
options: Add a new key for posture findings

decisions.topic: NEED: preventive guardrails at the top of the hierarchy (reconciliation)
decisions.question: Match or add a key for 'preventive guardrails that block public storage, long lived machine keys and grants to outside identities are enforced at the top of the hierarchy' (organisation policies on Google Cloud, service control policies on AWS, Azure Policy deny on Azure). aws.md lists service control policy checks as not proposed (YAGNI until a control asks).
decisions.source: connectors/gcp.md 5.3 (NS-04.B operating side of approved-configuration-baseline, IAM-10.D); connectors/aws.md section 5.2 'Not proposed'

decisions.topic: NEED: log of branch protection changes over the period (reconciliation)
decisions.question: GitLab Premium group audit events (and the GitHub Enterprise Cloud audit log) can show a protected branch or approval rule was not changed during the period. No artifact asks for it: 'NEED version_control: a log of changes to branch protection and approval rules over the period' (supports SD-06.C 'throughout the period'). Add an artifact and a check?
options: Add an artifact and a version_control check
Leave: daily reads are the history

defects.finding: The built GitHub connector does not read a ruleset's bypass list (the connector README says so), so the check can pass on a ruleset that every admin bypasses.
defects.proposal: Read GET /repos/{o}/{r}/rulesets/{id} (Metadata read) and add vcs.protection_bypass_limited.

defects.finding: Direct pushes to the default branch are not looked for: the check reads merged pull requests only, so it can pass while unreviewed code reached the branch (empty is not proof).
defects.proposal: Read rule suites (GET /repos/{o}/{r}/rulesets/rule-suites, Administration read, rule_suite_result=bypass, up to a month) and, only if D-GH-3 accepts Contents read, default branch commits not linked to a pull request; feed both into vcs.unreviewed_merges_recorded. Until then the result should say 'every pull request was reviewed'.

existing_check_changes.rationale: Extractor observation: the shipped description requires default branch or tag deploys AND a named approver, but github.md's predicate passes on required reviewers OR protected branch rules (a Team customer passes with no person approving), gitlab.md requires protection, limited deploy access AND an approval, and bitbucket.md requires limited users AND named branches. Align the description and predicate across providers, and leave the per deployment approval to ci.production_deploys_approved.

extra_notes: aws.md section 5.2 'Not proposed (YAGNI until a control asks)': service control policy checks, IMDSv2, Inspector coverage (that is scanner. and Phase 3), Macie, IAM password policy (idp.password_policy covers people signing in through the identity provider).

Shared cloud outcome rules (aws.md section 5, reused by azure.md and gcp.md): error on a denied call or unreachable service; insufficient_information when an account, Region, subscription or project was unread, paging was cut, or throttling stopped the run; not_applicable only when everything was read and the type is absent. A service the check asks for that is off is a fail (GuardDuty off fails cloud.threat_detection); a service read only as a source that is off is an error with reason 'not turned on' (Security Hub CSPM off for cloud.hardening_baseline). Recorded exceptions pass only until expiry and are printed. Thresholds come from connection settings: allowed public ports 80 and 443, database ports, key age 90, unused credential age 90, backup retention 7, log retention 365, finding response time 7 days, severity high.

Version control outcome rules (github.md section 5, reused by gitlab.md and bitbucket.md): a feature the plan or tier does not offer is fail with reason plan and the ways out; not_applicable for an empty repository; event checks use a 30 day window; caps 300 repositories and 100 merged changes per repository per run.

What clouds can never prove (aws.md section 6): NS-03.D, NS-07.C, NS-06.C (reviews), NS-05.C (the triage decision), BC-02.C (restore completeness), LM-03.C and LM-03.D (investigations, root causes), and every .A design objective.

What GitHub data can never prove (github.md section 6): every .A design objective, SD-04.E (management review of emergency rates), SD-10 (secure development design reviews and training), SD-14.D (retention), and the human halves named per check.

Bitbucket without D-BB-1 (bitbucket.md section 6): SD-06.C and SD-02.B stay with a person's dated export of branch restrictions; with D-BB-1 it also fills branch-protection-settings. A Bitbucket only customer has people's evidence for SD-03, SD-05 and SD-11.
Delivery phases: AWS Phase 2 (signed 'AWS (core cloud)'); Azure and Google Cloud Phase 3; GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket Cloud Phase 2 (Bitbucket Data Center out of scope). This matches capabilities.json.

Comparable platforms: Vanta, Drata, Sprinto (and Scrut, unverified) all use an AWS role with external ID and SecurityAudit; none offers a custom least privilege policy by default. Vanta uses a read only GitHub App and does not collect GitHub Actions or CI/CD data. Drata, Secureframe and Sprinto were not read for Azure, Google Cloud, GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket this round.
